headline: Iranian Rial Hits Record Low Following New US Sanctions
summary: The Iranian rial plunged to a record low of 2.856 million per dollar on the open market. The decline follows fresh US sanctions targeting Iranian exchange houses and companies accused of operating a 'shadow banking' network.
why: Currency devaluation in Iran exacerbates domestic inflation and complicates international trade, reflecting the impact of geopolitical tensions on the local economy.
why_moved: Sanctions on exchange houses and financial networks limit the availability of hard currency, driving up the black market exchange rate.
